source.title: Predicting Large Model Test Losses with a Noisy Quadratic System

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates the Chinchilla Method 3 loss model against held-out pretraining losses, using the same model and loss-prediction approach on new model runs as well as the original Hoffmann data.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports Chinchilla prediction fit and held-out prediction errors, and separately reports fitted NQS parameters across optimizer/schedule settings. NQS prediction scores are included as findings about an alternative loss-prediction model, not as evidence that a power law itself predicts well. The paper also reports compound-resource allocation results, but those do not test whether compute-optimal parameter and token counts follow stable powers of compute. Cited results from other works are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study refits Chinchilla Method 3, a power-law loss in N and D, with the Besiroglu et al. procedure. It fits on low-compute runs and scores predictions on held-out higher-compute runs, on Hoffmann's data and on new Pythia+OWT2 and Llama+LM1B runs. This directly tests V2 and touches V1 and V7. The framing ('Chinchilla Method 3 is not a great predictive model') also has a T5 character.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that Chinchilla Method 3 fits well in-distribution but is a poor predictive model beyond about x20 compute extrapolation. They argue for mechanistic loss models such as NQS over heuristic scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates Chinchilla Method 3 using the inference approach from Besiroglu et al. and reports results on both Hoffmann data and new Pythia + OWT2 and Llama + LM1B runs. The paper also proposes a different, mechanistic NQS loss model.
record.method_sensitivity: Chinchilla prediction results vary with fitting optimizer (L-BFGS versus TRF) and with the fitting dataset (IsoFLOPs alone versus IsoFLOPs plus B/K variation). The fitted NQS p, q, and r values differ between SGD + Constant LR and Adam + Cosine LR.

fits_no_version.finding: NQS, a mechanistic loss model in N, B and K, has lower holdout error than Chinchilla at x1024, x64 and x6 gaps. It stays accurate up to about a x4000 gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A mechanistic loss model including batch size and update count extrapolates held-out LM loss across compute better than the Chinchilla power law.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss varies with batch size at fixed N and D (B-K Plane), which a pure N,D power law cannot capture. Chinchilla's errors on these points are high (9.8, 8.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Power laws in N and D alone omit batch-size effects on loss at fixed token budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted NQS parameters differ between SGD + Constant LR and Adam + Cosine LR runs (q 0.70 vs 0.59, r 2.3 vs 1.5). The implied power-law exponents (p-1, about 0.13; (p-1)/q, about 0.20) are nearly unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer and schedule change NQS noise and spectrum parameters while leaving the implied N and D exponents roughly stable.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says implementation is available on GitHub but gives no URL in the text.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reported model families are limited in size (Pythia-like models up to 2B and Llama-like models up to 0.5B), and the Llama + LM1B compute gap is only ×6. The paper notes the fitting method does not jointly optimize the LayerNorm adjustment parameter s with the other NQS parameters, reports numerical issues for that gradient, and says NQS predictions are more sensitive to the initial learning rate than the LLMs. Some extrapolation comparisons are qualitative or presented in figures rather than as exact numerical errors.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Loss is not examined separately against N, D or compute with the others non-bottlenecked. The only shape evidence is the in-distribution fit quality of Chinchilla's joint N,D form.
Only up to 2B-parameter Pythia-like and 0.5B Llama-like models, plus Hoffmann's data. No frontier-scale extrapolation.
Untested. The Fig. 5 compound-constraint selection uses NQS and does not test how the optimal N and D scale with compute.
No fitted Chinchilla exponents or compute-optimal splits are reported under different fitting choices. Only holdout error changes are shown.

missing.what: Chinchilla vs NQS errors measured by MSE in log loss (units 1e-3). Chinchilla Train/Holdout: 0.2/9.1 at x1024, 0.3/4.6 at x64, 0.0/2.0 for Llama at x6. These show a larger relative gap than the Huber metric.
Chinchilla Train-set errors (0.8, 1.0, 0.7) as in-distribution fit and as baselines for the holdout rows.
Chinchilla extrapolation error as the compute gap grows on Hoffmann's original data (trend reported, figure only).

record.verdict_notes: The Chinchilla form originates in an original source, but this study is not itself one, so verdicts are allowed. B-K Plane rows are relinked to none because the N,D law cannot represent batch size. The NQS parameter rows r14-r19 (with r17-r19 duplicating r14-r16) are relinked to none: they are NQS parameters, and their implied exponents are stable, contrary to the reader's V7 'supports' label. The paper's stated compute gaps are internally a bit inconsistent (F.2 says the IsoFLOPs span is 4^8, Table 1 says x1024).

versions.untested_parts: Does not separately test loss versus parameters, tokens, and compute while holding the other quantities non-bottlenecked; the main tests concern fitted loss-model predictions over IsoFLOPs data and held-out compute.
Tests Chinchilla Method 3 extrapolation on the stated model families and compute gaps, not on arbitrarily larger models or other architectures.

The paper selects configurations under resource constraints and says selected configurations are close to ground-truth optimal, but does not test whether optimal parameter and token counts each grow as stable powers of compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No tests of other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.

Tests fitted NQS parameters across two optimizer/schedule configurations and reports Chinchilla prediction results under different fitting choices; it does not establish broad disagreement among published exponents or test dependence of the compute-optimal split.
